newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tapie quizzed over French lottery scandal.
newsitem.headline: Tapie quizzed over French lottery scandal.

text.p: Bankrupt French businessman and ex-soccer boss Bernard Tapie, serving a prison term for rigging a match, was questioned on Wednesday about a suspected lottery scandal, judicial sources said.

The sources, confirming a report in the newspaper Le Monde, said the former chairman of Marseille soccer club was taken from his cell at the Luynes jail in southern France for questioning as a witness.

Tapie was being quizzed about allegations that private television station TF1 paid a 10 million franc ($1.77 million) bribe in 1990 to the ex-head of France's lottery monopoly, Gerard Cole, to let TF1 keep its right to broadcast the lottery draw.

Le Monde said investigators considered Tapie, once a cabinet minister in a Socialist-led government, was a possible key witness in relation to suspicions that Cole, a friend of his, had received the cash.
Cole, a former aide to late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand, was placed under investigation in 1994. He and TF1 have denied the allegations.

Tapie, who says he has been the innocent victim of a political witchhunt in France, has been in jail since February 3, serving an eight-month sentence for rigging a league soccer match between Marseille and Valenciennes in 1993.
